name: From one's own work to entering the Lord (BhG 18.45–56)

stages.name: own work as worship (svakarma)
stages.gloss: devotion to one's own work, worshipping with it him who pervades all
stages.description: Devoted each to his own work a person attains perfection by worshipping with it him from whom beings arise (18.45–46); one's own dharma is kept though deficient (18.47–48).

stages.name: naiṣkarmya-siddhi
stages.gloss: the supreme perfection of freedom from action
stages.description: With understanding unattached everywhere, self-mastered, free of longing, one attains it through renunciation (18.49).

stages.name: the discipline fitting one for Brahman
stages.gloss: purified understanding, restraint, solitude, light food, dhyāna-yoga, dispassion, letting go of ahaṅkāra and possessions
stages.description: How the perfected one attains Brahman (18.50): the discipline of 18.51–53, ending in fitness for becoming Brahman (brahma-bhūya).

stages.name: brahmabhūta
stages.description: Serene, neither grieving nor craving, the same toward all beings (18.54a).

stages.name: parā bhakti; knowing the Lord in truth
stages.description: The one become Brahman attains supreme devotion, by which he knows the Lord — how great and who he is — in truth (18.54b–55a).

stages.name: entering the Lord; the eternal state
stages.gloss: entering thereafter; the eternal, imperishable state by grace
stages.description: Having known him in truth he enters him thereafter (18.55b); the one who takes refuge in the Lord attains by grace the eternal, imperishable state even while acting (18.56).

notes: Stages and their order are the text's (18.45–56); the bands are an interpretive alignment. 18.56 may describe a parallel route (refuge while acting) rather than a further stage; the text does not say.
